messages:
Maya (AE): Heads up: Prospect 'DeltaSys' wants a 2-week sandbox POC for a customer support assistant. They plan to test a community model variant 'delta-instruct-15b-quant-v2' plus some prompt injections. Can we confirm run compatibility and a quick est. cost?
Omar (Infra): Should be runnable on sandbox. Main things to check: tokenizer compat, KV cache warm-up (we've seen different warmup curves on v2), and effective batch size. Memory ~34-38GB on A100s.
Maya (AE): They included a security questionnaire and asked about certs, KMS/tenant isolation, and logging retention. Need answers by EOD Fri.
Priya (Security): Quick notes: we can provide KMS integration details, per-tenant audit logs, and VPC/private deploy options. For certs we can share our SOC2/ISO page. For model provenance, if variant came from vendor we can include provenance; if custom weights, we require legal review.
Lars (Solutions): I'll draft a one-page compatibility summary: recommended batch sizes (4-8), recommended max_seq 1024 for POC, and note on quant artifacts. Also will include a tiny smoke test curl + KV warmup script.
Maya (AE): Pricing ask: expected ~1.5M tokens/day during POC; what's hosted shared vs dedicated commit? Also does quant variant affect per-token billing?
Omar (Infra): Token billing unchanged. Quant affects GPU footprint & therefore per-req infra cost. Ballpark hosted shared POC = $0.10/k tokens for this variant; dedicated commit ~35-45% discount depending on term. I'll fetch exact numbers from pricing sheet and post.
Priya (Security): They also asked whether we can redact PII/PHI at ingestion. We can recommend our ingestion redaction rules and pointer to Console settings; full auto-redaction needs custom pipeline (we can propose splunk/processor integration).
Maya (AE): Great. Can we provide a short runbook for DeltaSys engineers to replicate results? They want to run it themselves in sandbox.
Lars (Solutions): Yes. I'll paste two commands: one curl for inference, one python script for KV warmup.
Lars (Solutions): curl example:

```bash
curl -X POST https://sandbox.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDWOOD-DELTA-POC" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"delta-instruct-15b-quant-v2","prompt":"Summarize: ...","max_tokens":80}'
```

Lars (Solutions): KV warmup check:
`python tools/kv_warmup_check.py --model delta-instruct-15b-quant-v2 --context 1024 --runs 20`
Omar (Infra): I'll spin the quick smoke run and paste latency / mem numbers. infra-bot: sandbox-deltasys provisioned on cluster-a (A100), token REDWOOD-DELTA-POC, status READY.
Priya (Security): I'll draft SSQ answers for KMS, data residency, SSO, and logging. Note: sandbox has 7d retention; production default 30d (extendable).
Maya (AE): If we identify quality regressions on quant vs non-quant, can we pin fallback?
Omar (Infra): Yes — routing policy supports variant pinning and fallback. Example config: `route: delta-instruct-15b-quant-v2 -> fallback: delta-instruct-15b-v1`. No downtime for switch.
Lars (Solutions): Also recommend A/B run (500 samples) and human eval on edge cases. I'll include a CSV template for scoring.
Maya (AE): Tasks: Lars - compatibility doc + scripts. Omar - smoke run + pricing numbers. Priya - SSQ draft. I'll compile and send to DeltaSys. ETA tomorrow noon PT.
Omar (Infra): smoke run started, will post results in ~25m.
Maya (AE): Thanks team — tagging DeltaSys contact @wecc to coordinate kickoff once we send bundle.
Lars (Solutions): small note: quant-v2 had slightly different logits scaling; include advice to normalize and run calibration on 100 prompts.
Priya (Security): if they want attestation of model provenance we need legal sign-off; flagging that for Maya.
Maya (AE): Perfect. I'll open a quick ticked for legal if needed. Will post updates here. :thumbsup:
